summary: Bollinger County towersite acquired 1947-48 for a Conservation Commission lookout; by 2018 the 40-acre site was kept for a radio tower and a pine stand.

facts.status_note: Listed on the former-sites register; no source gives a removal date. A 2006 visit report still mentions a tower; the 2018 MDC plan describes only a radio tower.

access.note: MDC lists the 40-acre Gipsy Towersite with hours of 4:00 AM to 10:00 PM; directions run west of Route TT onto a private lane

events.note: Missouri Conservation Commission acquired a 40-acre towersite in fiscal 1947-48
September 1949 Mexico Ledger item calls the Grassy and Gipsy towers new; no build date given for this tower alone
Visit report: tower not actively used but still maintained; access road closed by locked gate
Registered March 16, 2015 as US 1594, MO 2; nominated by Jerry Lutes
MDC area plan: site historically used for wildfire detection and establishment of a radio tower; purpose now is maintaining the radio tower for communications

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register and the brief spell the site Gypsy; the MDC pages, the 1949 Ledger quotes and the Forest Lookouts page spell it Gipsy. The story uses Gipsy for the site and notes the register spelling.

The 2006 visit report refers to a tower on the site, while the 2018 MDC plan describes only a radio tower and no lookout. The brief's gone status is kept because the site is listed on the former-sites register, but no source dates the removal.

notes_for_editor: No source gives staffing, fire history, the lookout's height or design, or the year the lookout came down, so those are left out. The 2008 Southeast Missourian blog returned 403 and a Facebook MCC post returned no text, so neither was used. The tower's build year is inferred only from the 1949 'new towers' wording. The Mexico Ledger date is taken from the Forest Lookouts quote. The brief's 'gone' status rests on the former-sites listing alone.
